  PROBLEM: `_append_semble_block` and `_append_read_fallback_block` charge only source content against `used_bytes`, while framing lines are appended outside the budget.
  WHY: With many overflow entries, framing overhead can push the block past `max_bytes`, contradicting the documented hard-budget claim; the severity was reported as MAJOR by qwen_qwen3_7-plus and NIT by deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, so the highest severity is used.

  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The README row for `TARGETED_FILE_CONTEXT_MAX_BYTES` claims the block cannot exceed the budget despite uncharged framing overhead.
  WHY: Operators may set the limit too close to the stdin cap and the emitted block can exceed it; severity was reported as MAJOR.
- tests/test_targeted_file_context.py: line 773 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The test asserts only `assert len(context.encode("utf-8")) < 102400` instead of verifying the documented source-content budget and bounded framing overhead.
  WHY: The test does not validate the actual contract; severity was reported as MAJOR.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml: lines 2022-2036 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The log line compares codex stdin cap in characters to `wc -c` output in bytes without stating the unit mismatch.
  WHY: The conservative comparison can produce false warnings for multibyte prompts and erode trust in the guard.
